utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I understand there is something to be raised by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone, good afternoon, your Excellencies. Well, here is the thing. This Chamber has adopted a rule that it is permissible to speak and tender evidence relating to the incidents not scheduled within the indictment, particularly if they refer to the Bihac, Gorazde, Tuzla and other protected areas. This is the single witness with whom I can clarify fully the matter of how they investigated modified air-bombs, how they investigated the Markale case and particularly how they investigated the incident that took place in Tuzla known as Kapija. This last incident was referred to by General Smith as well, and by this witness. He's the only one with whom I can clarify this, among the OTP witnesses, relating to the military industry in Sarajevo, because that was part of the military industry complex. As far as Tuzla is concerned, this witness knew that that was an example that completely discredited their methods and he even said that publicly in the media. He said that he anticipated and was afraid that Karadzic will use the example of Tuzla and the approach thereto in order to discredit him as a witness. I was given 25 hours -- I was given.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: I was given six hours for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I need 25 because there is no other way, if I don't have an opportunity to question and examine this witness about each particular circumstance and demonstrate that not only their model, but his model of reaching conclusion as well, was erroneous. He's appearing here as a Prosecution witness, but I am denied the opportunity to fully reveal what his expertise and his testimony is about. Therefore, I kindly ask to you grant me additional time. Otherwise there is no other option than to call him again, and I think it's better if we did that while he is still here. Whatever you decide, I would gladly accept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Give me a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Bear with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At this time, Mr. Gaynor, the Chamber does not feel it necessary to get your assistance on this matter. Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber is not prepared to extend the time for your cross-examination. There is one technical matter --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say for the record that I will then consider that this witness hasn't been examined. If the Chamber decides to discount this witness in totality, then that would be a different thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has given its ruling. With reference to our decision on the accused's motion to reclassify as public contained -- the contained portions of the transcript relating to Berko Zecevic filed yesterday I would like to note that that decision also applies to the audiovisual record of those portions, and instruct the Registry to make the portions of the audiovisual record, which correspond to the transcript pages referred to in the decision, public. I take it there is a matter for you to raise, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Very quickly, it concerns the accused's motion for a binding order to the United Nations. The Court will have, I believe, by this time, received a letter from a UN representative seeking additional time in light of the extraordinary demands on their office in view of recent international events. I spoke with Mr. Robinson about this. I understand from him he has no objection to that request for an extension of time or to a corollary request that we would make orally now, that the Prosecution's submissions be filed the day after the Court receives the UN submissions, which would be March 3rd, if their request was granted. So they would file on March 3rd, according to that we would file on March 4th, as against the Defence has no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we grant the OTP a further extension of its deadline to 4th of March, and we note that we anticipate receiving the United Nations submissions on 3 March.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's consistent with my understanding of the request that was -- that should have been received today or was sent yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I would ask the Chamber's legal officer to communicate that to the United Nations. With respect to your for authorisation to exceed the word limit to 4.500 words, do you have any observation, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That is granted. Taking advantage of the absence of the witness, I have some minor matters, several matters, to deal with in relation to binding order. In relation to the second binding order to Bosnia and Herzegovina, I think is it 9 February, Bosnia-Herzegovina sent correspondence stating that it had delivered the request. Also, could you update us on that issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We haven't received anything from them. I believe their communication exhibited a willingness to get those materials before us, but they haven't done that yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So if you could let us know as soon as you receive some.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about Denmark?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we have made some progress with Denmark. The United Nations authorised us to interview the two officers. We requested an appointment for the 21st of February but they weren't available. We have now requested another appointment for the 1st of April and waiting to hear if those officers will be available, but it seems we are reaching a conclusion. As soon as they have been interviewed, if we are satisfied that Denmark has no additional materials, we'll withdraw the binding order motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robinson. Shall we go into private session, briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we are doing that I notice that the Chamber's artillery expert is not present today so I assume you're sitting under Rule 15 bis, and I hope it's not for any ill health by Judge Morrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for reminding us of that point. Yes, we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. He's away on official business. So he will join us tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Zecevic. Please make yourself comfortable. Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we started a conversation about the Markale case. After the investigation carried out by your commission, you compiled your report in which, under item 9 of the conclusions, the following is said. Do you need the document in front of you now? Can we have 65 ter 10676, page 13 in the Serbian version? So 65 ter 10676, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2317, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The entire conclusion is important but you said here explicitly everything that you said. Item 9 reads as follows: "In the territory under the control of the BH Army, is one area of the possible origin of fire, and there are five such areas of possible fire on the aggressor's side."

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That means what your commission reached an identical conclusion as that reached by UNPROFOR, which is to say that it was not possible to determine exactly where the shell had come from; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is said here that there are six potential locations from which this projectile could have been fired, and at that moment, and in the role -- the report that I wrote, I listed these six locations. As a result of later analysis, at the request of the OTP, I identified three locations as potential places from which the projectile was fired. However, in those times, when I and my colleagues conducted our work, this was the best conclusion that we could have come up with. So I explained explicitly in my testimony here that the presence of the stabiliser embedded in the ground clearly indicates that the locations of the potential fire are 4.950 to 6400 metres from the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, in your conclusion, you said the "possible" origin of fire. You didn't say you explicitly which location you had in mind; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The six probable locations from which theoretically the fire could have come. However, the subsequent analysis of the stabiliser reduced this to three possible locations of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you carry out this additional analysis?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why did you do it?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that was for the General Galic trial and the immediate cause was when a group of experts from the Military Technical Institute, made up of the late Dr. Stamatovic, Dr. Ranko Vilicic and Milorad Vukasinovic, they were the ones who analysed the shelling of Sarajevo and the incidents relating to that, while I was asked by the OTP to provide a counter-analysis to the one that they made, and this is the first time that I identified these three locations in that analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time when you made this, you allowed for a possibility that the probability rate of around 16 -- 17 per cent indicates that the shell could have come from the Bosnian side. So you said one-third, and one-third is approximately 17 per cent; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Are you talking about point of impact?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, you made a contemporaneous conclusion that there were six possible locations of which 17 per cent could have been from the BH Army-controlled area and the rest were from the Serb-controlled areas?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic. That's not the way to apply statistics. Statistical methods can be used in a uniform and contained systems. Each of these locations were different systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So for the purpose of the Galic case, you carried out an additional analysis, taking into account the penetration, and drew a conclusion that certain distance that you mentioned today was involved?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman from the Military Technical Institute and I reached similar conclusions with regard to the penetration, and the velocity of ejection. We differed on some other aspects that I enumerated in my analysis, but it is beyond dispute that what I said clearly indicates the possible zones of launching at 4.950 to 6400 metres from the place of explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you do that in your first report, Mr. Zecevic? You rather did it 8 or 9 years later. Why this is not contained in this particular report but it rather allows for the possibility of the ratio of one to five?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking you. Why are you -- why didn't do you it immediately?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm waiting for the interpretation to be finished. I'm not hesitating because I can't give you an answer. We all agreed to be fair to our interpreters and I'm looking at the screen here to see when I can start my answer. I told you that I had limited time at my disposal, along with my associate, for the preparation of this analysis. That's one thing. Secondly, for such a complex analysis, one needs time and wisdom, because the situation in Sarajevo was so dramatic at the time that, quite simply, nothing was possible to be done within 36 hours. Given that after I had finished my analysis, I wasn't, so to speak, in a position to be within the circles in Sarajevo who would make it capable -- who make it possible for me to do something but I rather had to fight for survival with my family, it was only after the war that I continued working on these investigations and researches. As soon as I would gather any new information, I would provide it to the OTP. If you are accusing me of endeavouring to conceal what I knew, I think you're not right. At that time, this analysis is a reflection of my findings and my capabilities available to me at the time. As soon as I had different circumstances of living in peace, I did what I did. Of course, my analysis can be the subject of criticism by anyone who wishes to do so. So there is no ill intention on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. This is exactly what I'm doing. I'm trying to test your findings. So several years later, you are trying to rectify certain things that the OTP is not satisfied with, that is the Hrasnica case, the Markale case, that's the Tuzla case, et cetera. Is that correct? So years later, you amended the evidence because they were not satisfied with the previous evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection to the characterisation that he's trying to rectify certain things that the OTP is not satisfied with. I believe that's an improper suggestion to make and it's not founded. He hasn't made any prima facie case that the OTP is dissatisfied with any of the findings made by Dr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is he not entitled to put his case?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, he is entitled to put his case, but he cannot assume a matter that is not in evidence in any question, in my submission. Specifically it hasn't emerged that the OTP has been dissatisfied in any way with the analyses provided by Dr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If this is indeed part of Defence case, we will allow the question to be put, but before that, I have to confirm that whether it is your part of the case, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to this expertise, yes, it is. I did not say OTP. I said Prosecutor's offices or Prosecutor's office, referring to the office in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I will prove my point. You will -- you give me more time, I will be able to show you what I am going for. So you will see as I continue that it is correct. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember the question, Dr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do remember the question. Will you permit me to answer it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means, Dr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I conducted this analysis in 1994 and I handed it over not to the Prosecutor's office but to the investigating judge. I don't know what happened with the analysis after that. I made the analysis for the action of the projectile on the television building. I handed it over to the investigating judge and later I found out that the analysis was not sent to the OTP in The Hague but that it was put to one side somewhere. I worked on the analysis for the Kapija case at the request of the state prosecutor's office of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I don't know what the Prosecution did in terms of that, who worked on that, I got material and on the basis of that material I carried out my work. I did not make any corrections of the reports or studies, any other ones, so I completely reject the idea that I could have falsified anything or could have tried to use any kind of impermissible means. This is not something that is inherent in the way I work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, is it correct that for all of those cases, the Bosnia-Herzegovina Prosecutor's office had the investigation material, tempore criminis, made at the time of the incident. For Hrasnica, the direction that was established was north; is that correct, but then 13 years later, you came and you said, no, it's not the north; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just say "yes" or "no", there is no need to go into anything else.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never submit to any kind of pressure, in any case, and to anyone. If we are here at a court that I am exceptionally respectful of, then I seek the right to express my opinion. If I'm not given that right from this point on, I will stop speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, I have the right to put questions to you. Was there any material that was created at the point in time of the incident indicating that the incoming direction of the projectile was the north?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I received the material from The Hague Prosecutor's office. They asked for my opinion; they wanted to see what my position on that was. I gave them my position. I don't work according to the copy-paste system. I'm not interested in what the investigating organs did. I went to the scene of the incident myself. I established every element for myself. I spoke to everyone. I carried out the analysis. I assessed what was all right and what was not all right, and pursuant to that, I wrote my opinion. As to whether that opinion is correct or not, it is subject to criticism, but that is how I work. I am responsible for my work. I'm not responsible for the work of others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Zecevic. Let us move our doubt to the Prosecutor's office. The Prosecutor's office in Sarajevo had findings about Hrasnica. You didn't ask for anything else. You actually asked for Tuzla. Did the Bosnia OTP have findings for Tuzla which were created at the time of the incident in Tuzla, when it occurred?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's wait a little bit first. When they called me, they gave me the complete documentation, which contained their investigative organ's report and the UNPROFOR report. At the time it also included the photo file and that was the basis that I used in order to carry out my own analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After Galic or before Galic, did you testify in President Milosevic's case?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified in President Milosevic's case after testifying in the Galic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On 16 January, 1994, you said this in the President Milosevic case. I will provide the reference in the e-court. "We established only six locations, the conclusion is only six locations, one of the B and H army and five of the VRS, nothing more." So in January 2004, you did not have anything more than these six possibilities, is that what you said at the time?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I said that correctly, because that refers to the analysis that was conducted in 1994. And in the analysis that I did in January 2003, for the Prosecutor's office, I acquired some new insight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And why didn't you say that in January 2004 in the case against President Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It's just a minor mistake by the accused where he said 16 January 1994a few lines ago. He meant 16 January 2004. I think that's clear. Just to make sure the transcript is easy to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2004, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic, can you continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just answering the questions that were put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. So the new analysis was carried out for the Galic case in 2003. In the case against Milosevic in January 2004, you still said, "We established six possible locations." Nothing else, not a word more that was yours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that reflects in its entirety what was the conclusion from the report of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your conclusion, paragraph 10, you also said, let's look at the documents, potentially destructive power of the projectile at the target corresponds to the number of victims and type of injuries they suffered in the massacre; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said, in the case against President Milosevic, and this is page -- actually, it's 1D3316, this has been admitted now, we can remove it, 1D3316, page 63 in the e-court. If necessary, perhaps it won't be necessary for us to call it up. You responded like this, "Mr. Milosevic, I -- Mr. Milosevic, I applied or reported in because so many of my citizens were killed and so many were wounded --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true Mr. Zecevic that a total of 332 people were killed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The numbers are 68 were killed, 260 were wounded. So this shell, is it possible that this shell, fatally or non-fatally, struck a total of 332 persons?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, 68 killed and 200 something wounded, I think it was 150 people that were wounded. That is more realistic. I beg your pardon, no, actually I couldn't give you a precise answer. I don't have the material in order to be able to answer this. There was a large number of dead and there was a large number of wounded. What's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The problem is that you said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's time to take a five-minutes break. We are taking a five-minutes break every 25 minutes to accommodate the situation of the witness. Five minutes. --- Break taken at 2.10 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this page, at line 18, you say that you volunteered because 68 of your fellow citizens were killed and 274 were wounded. This is more than 342 citizens were, fatally, and the others non-fatally, hurt by this shell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say it?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I probably said it. I mean, if it's in the transcript. But that doesn't mean anything. The city knows exactly how many people were killed, how many people were wounded. That would be the definite figure. It doesn't matter what I said because later I found out that this number included persons who were wounded by other firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But it's important to us what you say. We know what happened but it's important what you say to us as well. You said that 342 people were killed, we are going to come back to that, because you are an expert on the effects at the place of impact. Is it correct that you did not say whether the number of victims corresponds to the possible number of people who were in the market?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, is it correct that every person who happened to be at the market was hit? Is that your opinion?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there were more than 342 people at the market at that time, is that possible?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it's possible. Why wouldn't there be more than that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you establish what the space was between the stalls and could you estimate on the basis of that what the possible number of people in the market was?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, a person takes up half a square metre when they are standing up, the surface of the market is about 25 by 34, 40, 45 metres. Maybe more. Maybe less. I really am not quite sure. I can't give you an exact picture. Maybe you will allow me to make that calculation. At the time when they asked me, there was no need for me to make that calculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at 1D3293, please? This is the sketch. And then it will make it easier for you to tell us what you are trying to say. 1D3293 in the e-court, please. Can we zoom up on the top part? Is that your sketch or is that a diagram that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 11.1 metres by 4.16 ... Yes, this is my diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we zoom in a little tighter, please? This is called, "The radial distribution of fragments for the 120-millimetre mine." This is the title of the diagram; is that correct? Can we scroll up a little bit? Because Mr. Zecevic then can see what the title is of the diagram.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sketch is called the area of the Markale Market, and it shows the radius, which is about -- which is 17 metres, I think this is the effective action radius of a 120-millimetre mortar, which is in the firing tables of the JNA, according to which each person that finds themselves in this zone statistically speaking would at least be hit by one fragment of a 100-joule energy unit. This is the standard. Later this standard was reduced to 80. This area R equals 24 metres is the area in which the probability of a person getting -- or in which the probability is 2 persons would be hit by one fragment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this. The northern building and the eastern building that are in this radius, is it correct that they absorbed over 50 per cent of the blast and that the market is affected by only one-quarter of this energy as indicated by this cut in the -- in the square?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it's a little bit more than a quarter. It's a third. Perhaps slightly more. Because what you need to take into account is also this area here towards the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So over one-third of the blast was directed at the people in the market, and the neighbouring buildings absorbed slightly less than two-thirds of this blast energy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not how it is. You need to be clear about one thing. The radius of the kill power is worked out on the basis of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is kindly asked to repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters couldn't hear your last answer, the last bit of it. Could you complete that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lethal power radius is a statistical value, which is worked out according to standards of the Yugoslav People's Army, and it's a value that is used in the serial production in order to show whether the efficacy of the projectile corresponds to the requirements in the manufacture of that projectile. So the comparison is made on the basis of similar projectiles, and this is tested in the following way: The projectile is placed in a vertical position with the fuse at the bottom, with the assumption that the fragments will disperse equally on all sides. In a real situation, the projectile will strike the surface at some kind of angle, and then we will get a completely different picture. And at the same time, in real -- in a real situation, a ricochet will occur, which, in the testing conditions of the effective range radius, is strictly forbidden. So in the case that we have as in the Markale case, an asphalt surface, and a lot of metal surfaces, stone surfaces, what will happen is that the fragments will ricochet and they will be redirected to completely different areas in relation to the results that were recorded during testing of the lethal action radius.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is no doubt that this northern area marked with 195 and 167, that these are buildings on the diagram?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No doubt about that. Fragments will enter the area or the vertical plane and will not cause a ricochet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to your findings, did this mine explode on the ground or on a stall?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my findings, the projectile impacted on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The stalls, did they absorb a certain number of fragments and were they a barrier on the path of these fragments?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stalls were made of pipes, metal pipes, right? With wood panelling, and they are not very thick, if I can put it that way. It is only logical that if a fragment encounters any obstacle or a barrier, it will decrease its velocity and change the direction in which it is moving. That is to say, if it can ricochet in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you are an expert for what happens at the point of impact, are you trying to say that at this 24-metre segment, 115 degrees, that 342 persons were grazed or hit?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Fragments have a velocity of 1200 metres per second. I have already said to you that as for people who are not in this line of work, this figure doesn't mean anything. But if you say that it is 30 metres per second, is 108 kilometres per hour, then you can imagine that that is 40 times this velocity at which the fragments leave the point of explosion. If you take into account the fact that it is the square of the velocity that is this energy, then you come to the conclusion that these fragments can either kill a person or cut this person's veins or legs or whatever. So an analysis that would lead to minimising the effects of the action of a mortar projectile that hit a marketplace smack in the middle of it, that is a disgrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you document the condition in which these stalls were, whether there were any fragments left in the wood panelling and in the stalls as such?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I -- I have already said to you that I came a day later, and that on the scene did I not find the situation as it had been originally. What I saw was that at certain metal -- on certain metal pipes, fragments had penetrated through them. They did not just hit them and stick inside. From the investigation team I got some photographs of what they had found on the scene. And that is what I included in my documentation of 2003 that I handed over to the OTP. I don't know whether they used it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing. Did you draw this diagram?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't draw it, but I did the measurements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you set the cardinal points here?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. It was the investigator who did, not me, but I was present when he did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't have a compass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'd like to show you some footage, that is 1451. It's a Prosecution exhibit from 017 to 019.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Before we get there, Mr. President I just want to check if the accused intends to tender the map that we've just looked at. If he doesn't, I can raise it in redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it part of his report? I couldn't find it in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, it's not part of his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we -- are you tendering it? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it hasn't been admitted, if it's not part of the report, then I would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted as Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D1095, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, let us have a look -- is this the 5th of February 1994? Can we see that on the screen, the 5th of February 1994 so then can we just play these few seconds?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you kindly to observe the red box and the entire scene.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D3294? It's a still from this footage. It's the first image that we saw. 1D3294.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the place where the explosion took place here?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Mr. Zecevic's pen please be activated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can say with any reliability on the basis of this footage --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please place number 1 there?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now mark the damage on this red box, the damage caused by the fragments?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain this, that fragments caused damage there and the point of explosion was over there?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These fragments would have to behave like a boomerang. They would have to go around the corner.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if they hit metal or stone but this is ten-millimetre thick wood. May I please continue? A fragment that is at a distance of, say, three metres, went through this wood just like a knife goes through butter, no problem. You see, when we are investigating the fragmentation of this projectile, we place the projectile this way and we tie it to a wooden pole so that it's a vector. Ten metres away we place a sector. That is semi-circular panelling, 25 millimetres thick, made of pine wood, and then at a distance of 20 metres and then 30 metres and then 40 metres. When an explosion takes place, at 30 metres and at 40 metres, you are going to see that fragments passed through this pine wood plank, 25 millimetres thick. So what I see here is simply a -- the last part of the fragments that passed through this wooden plank. No problem whatsoever. It is going to ricochet if it hits concrete and then again it depends under which angle or if it hits steel plate, but a wooden panel is no problem whatsoever. I mean that question is really --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. So you claim that it passed on the front through this box and then went out through the other side?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can assume that, Mr. Karadzic, because this is a photograph. I cannot enter a photograph. I don't have a 3-D photograph, therefore I cannot see. At that time there were no 3-D photographs yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please sign this and put the date.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. What's the date today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 24th.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D1096.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have P1452 from 7.11 to 7.14?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D3295. Can we have that photograph now? It's a photograph of the first image we saw. 1D3295, can we have that, please? Mr. Zecevic, is this the point of impact of that projectile?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where is the tail-fin at this point, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably at the intersection point of these two elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you explain that this point of impact has been filled with this rubble and this material?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very simply. Now I'm going to explain. Mr. President, Mr. President, may I show a photograph that was taken by the Americans and Germans about the fragmentation of a projectile? So that my explanation would be more illustrative. This is exceptionally important in view of this question of yours and it's very important for the Judges to understand on that basis what I'm saying. So it's not my photographs. This is an ultra-fast camera of 1 million images per second. They are not my photographs. And they fully explain what I'm about to describe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If there is enough time.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, this is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, please proceed. Shall we put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that my time stops right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In any event, Dr. Zecevic, we'll see it after the break. We'll have another five-minutes break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Agreed. --- Break taken at 2.40 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Robinson and Mr. Karadzic, that in answer to the question put by Mr. Karadzic, the witness is trying to explain some theory in technical terms, and in the course of explanation, that explanation, it is my understanding that the witness wishes to use a picture from a book. So do you have any observation, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't see any problem with that, Mr. President. If it's of value to the Chamber, it can also be admitted as a Chamber exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection to its use, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please proceed, doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. On this photograph here, we can see six sequences of the phase of fragmentation of a high-explosion projectile. The beginning and then already after 22.5 millionths of a second, the expansion of the casing starts and the procedure of fragmentation and the fuse is separated. The process of fragmentation continues and you see that certain parts of the body of the projectile do not move at the same speed. They have different speeds. The highest speed of the fragments is in the central part of this group. You can see that in all of these photographs. And the rear parts have a very small velocity. That is in accordance with what I tried to say, that the speed of ejecting the tail-fin is about 170 millimetres per second, is about 200 metres per second. If we look at the other photograph, we can see it in more specific terms. This is MK 42 which is very similar to FAP 250. We see the moment when the fragmentation takes place. However, you will note that this bomb expanded its diameter two or three times before a fragmentation occurred and that is exceptionally important. At the very beginning, you see that the products of detonation started to move at a very high velocity. That is the answer to Mr. Karadzic's question, why, in the zone of the point of impact, there is a certain amount of rubble, as Mr. Karadzic called it, or, rather, these are pieces of asphalt, sand, soil and so on, because the products of detonation, as they flow out of the place where the fuse was, they move 2, 3, 4, sometimes even 10 kilometres per second depending on the technical performance of the projectile. That would be my brief attempt to explain what it was that was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Zecevic, none of these are -- is 120-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is completely irrelevant. The analysis of high-explosive warhead is uniform. Actually, it depends on the type of the warhead, of whether it be a cruise missile or an artillery missile or any other type of missile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you show us here an aerosol bomb with solid fuel or air fuel?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a warhead with solid fuel, and I can show you the original photograph of a rocket-assisted aerosol bomb that is kept within the armed forces depot. I have very good photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm no longer interested in this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson suggested this to be admitted as Chamber exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think that it would be appropriate given that he's referred to them and otherwise the record wouldn't totally understand what he had referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it the Prosecution is minded to tender it as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's right as well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit it as a Prosecution exhibit. We will give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2323.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 2323. Very well. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, can you please pay attention now to e-court? The position of the Defence is that during first measurements and filming or photographing of the scene, the material did not flew away from the point of impact but that rather this place had been filled; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer? How can you ask me to give you an answer to that? Because I wasn't at the scene immediately after the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So at this stage of investigation, and photographing, you say that the stabiliser is inside the crater; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I said that only after, when I was viewing the footage of the extraction of the stabiliser by UNPROFOR soldiers and I stand by it. What happened before or after, I don't know. All I saw was this footage and it is clearly stated in my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zecevic, I'm kindly asking you and the interpreters to see or listen to what the investigations are saying. There is only one sentence involved and the interpreters have it. It's P7111, from 6.46. Let us please listen carefully to what this young investigator, he seems young, is saying.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could only hear it from the computer. Can we hear this voice in the system and I'm kindly asking the interpreters to interpret this one sentence. Could the technical staff please establish the connection again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will revert to the original way of translation. The translator will be coming into the courtroom. I was mistaken. A technician is coming inside to give assistance. Do you have any other objects to deal with in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We can look at a photograph taken from a videoclip, 1D3301. It's from a videoclip 3822-1-A. D0003822-1-A. It's again a Prosecution piece of material. That refers to what happened on the previous day, i.e. on the 4th of February 1992, in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, is this the usual appearance of a crater with the embedded stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I cannot identify this, because the resolution of the picture is very bad. I can only slightly discern that there is something in the ground, but I can't see the stabiliser. I can't confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, then, let's play the film, if necessary. Are you saying that this is not a stabiliser? Do you see all its elements?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I have my own eyes, you have your own eyes. I'm telling you what I can see, which means that I cannot give you a precise identification because the photograph is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this material, asphalt, and everything else resemble Markale?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, first of all, I cannot give you any statement about that, because I don't know whether there is a stabiliser inside the hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we please tender this photograph into evidence? We have the date, the 4th of February 1992, and the film is 0003822-1-A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Two observations, first of all, I think Dr. Karadzic means the 4th of February 1994. Ironically enough, the same date I was having trouble with yesterday. Second point is I don't believe that the witness has given any evidence to confirm the photograph that we've seen on the screen so far. So on that basis, it does not appear to be admissible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am tendering it with respect to the credibility of this witness. If the witness is unable to confirm whether this is a stabiliser or not, that speaks about his credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that this is part of the video, and in considering the witness's answer, that he can only slightly discern that there is something in the ground, but he can't see the stabiliser, I think there is a basis to admit this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will give it the next Defence Exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D1097.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we take a break now? It's time to take the half hour break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then we will take a half an hour break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, this is the place at the point in time when the investigation was carried out. Can we ask all participants to pay attention to the words of the investigator that accompany this video footage?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Can you look on the roof, please, to see if the tail-fin is not there, maybe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the investigator is saying, Go to the roof to check if the tail-fin is perhaps there?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and there is nothing strange about that. This is the proper procedure when an investigator is investigating the scene of the crime, compiling the documentation, doing all the proper investigative procedures and we'll see later that the UNPROFOR soldier will come and take a look and see where the stabiliser is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat his question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please wait, put a pause. The interpreter couldn't hear you. Could you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We've seen the photograph from Dobrinja from the day before on the same surface, what the crater looks like. Let me ask you this now. A little bit earlier you showed us the process of fragmentation. Would you agree that fragmentation precedes the penetration of the stabiliser into the surface?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that penetration takes place at a velocity of some 200 metres per second? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I remark on the interpretation? Actually, it does not occur at 200 metres per second if we are talking about the stabiliser fin. What do you mean when you say penetration of the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the sequence of physical actions. We have contact with the fuse, we have the explosion, and then the fragmentation. After that, the stabiliser fin continues to delve into the earth or it's ejected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well what you said is not quite precise, but let's say it is that way. Because at the point in time when the projectile strikes the obstacle, the explosive chain is initiated which lasts for a millionth part of a second, the explosive is activated, the process is not instantaneous. The body of the mine expands. The fuse is pushed towards the ground. The products of the detonation are released and the body continues to expand. There are cracks and then the fragmentation, the fragments disperse on all sides, to some 1.000 to 1200 metres per second, and then the stabiliser is embedded into the surface if the speed of the projectile at the point of impact is greater than 170 plus/minus 20 metres per second. If not, it will be ejected or it will drop somewhere in the vicinity. There are some variations, but we don't need to lose any more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just ask the interpreter possibly to check the use of the word "mine"? The word in the original does resemble the English word "mine," but it's usually translated as mortar and I do believe that Dr. Karadzic would accept that, that the word we are looking for is mortar rather than mine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mortar projectile.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mortar is the device and the projectile is the mortar mine or shell. In our language, the mortar is the barrel and the mine or the shell is the projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that clarifies the matter. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You ruled out the possibility in your report that the shell was thrown from the neighbouring roof or that it was activated in some other way; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please -- well, I said that that was not rational. It's not possible to throw a projectile with a fuse that is prepared for action for the projectile to fall on the tip or the head of the fuse, and for the fin then to embed itself into the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. In the report you said, I'm going to read it to you, that means that the velocity must act upon the shell in order for it to be armed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order for the fuse to be armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Without them, without these forces, it is just an inert object that is not going to explode. Thus this rules out the possibility of using a mortar shell in any other way than the one that it is meant for. Illustration. For example, if a shell were to be dropped from a building, the fuse would not be armed because the forces that would develop while it was falling would not activate the fuse arming mechanism; is this correct from your report?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please tell me which report you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was an interview with you, and then you said, "Then we asked Professor Zecevic." We will find it in just a minute, please. The ERN number is 03051467, 03051467. And it's paragraph 4, actually paragraph 5 on that page. Does this text sound familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I gave hundreds of interviews, and I really couldn't tell you when I gave the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will get the reference now. Perhaps the ERN number will help to find the correct text. During the examination-in-chief, you changed slightly what you said, and you said it would be possible to arm the fuse by hand in such a way that even a small impact can activate it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not in that way. Simply, while -- for military purposes, it is forbidden to make any kind of interventions on the fuse. But if you want to be a terrorist, this is something else. And you want to be a suicide bomber, and you want to kill your fellow citizens, then you are going to make interventions on the fuse or make a new fuse which will have no protective mechanisms and then you will stand on top of a building, you will take a mortar and throw the shell and watch as your fellow citizens are getting killed by you. You could do it like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. I wouldn't have described it better myself.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I mean, this is what terrorists do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Other than this modification that would be done on the fuse, could such a shell be activated in some other way? For example, by an explosive, like dynamite or some kind of electronic fuse or something?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking about a terrorist act again. Perhaps you can put your hypothesis of what a terrorist is supposed to do and then I could give you my expert opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, can this mine be activated by a dynamite stick or some other way?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, what you are assuming is that a terrorist would take a mortar projectile, place it on the market. In this case it would be the market, wouldn't it? Okay. Or perhaps a department store, would place it there, would place the detonator and the plastic explosive in order to create the initiation of the first charge, the primary charge, the activation could be carried out electronically, it would be by a slow-burning fuse, it could be by a detonating fuse, it could be by a radio-directed device. It's a question of choice. This is why you have terrorism all over the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's probably known to you that on the day of the incident, investigation teams of the UNPROFOR came to the scene of the crime and the French captain made a report which was later excluded from the analysis, because of some assessments of the direction that did not fit into the results of the other investigators. Regardless of the shortcomings, this captain's report is quite significant for another reason. He wrote in the report that the shell exploded on the market stall. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that, because nobody gave me such a report to read, and to tell you the truth, I'm not interested in reading other people's reports. For one reason only, and that is if I get a project of what I'm supposed to do, then I strictly stick to what is given to me to analyse. I always indicate that at the start of my analysis. And in that way, I can be quite certain that I did not have any outside influences during the forming of my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the number? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1441. P1441, page 1, please, and then can we look at page 5? Thank you. Can we see this document in the e-court? All right. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at page 1, please? And now can we look at page 5? Item G. Can we look at paragraph marked G, where it says, "Description of damage": [In English] "The mortar shell impacted on the wood of a stall, 90 millimetres from the ground so that the analysis was very difficult." [Interpretation] They didn't show you this, did they?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a P document, so we won't tender it. How would the explosion manifest itself if the explosion occurred on the stall?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us: Had the explosion happened on the stall, on the top of the stall, what would it have looked like?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer I want to give you a technical description of the stall. The stall has a plastic roof. Right? Do we agree? Underneath the stall, underneath the roof, about 1.20 metres lower there is a paper -- a wooden surface, and that surface is installed on a metal frame. Have I described a stall correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. The structure, but the dimensions are not quite accurate. But we will do that later.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectile would not be able to pass through the plastic roof without exploding, before hitting the wooden surface of the stall plate. And you can look at that. I gave the results of the French technical experts and this is the report with their findings, and it says that the mortar fuse can act on a cardboard surface that is 3 millimetres thick. So in any case, the mortar projectile could not explode on the table of the stall but it would be activated as soon as it hit the roof. So this finding actually is contrary even to the findings of the French experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think then that you assume that if the projectile was at an angle of 90 degrees, it would have to explode as soon as it hit the roof but if it came at an angle of 60 degrees or lower could it miss the roof and hit the stall directly?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you want me to answer that, Mr. Karadzic, I would like you to give me a diagram of that assumption because you are not -- you are not being precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you were indicating what the normal situation would be because you did mention the angle of 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the angle is less than 90 degrees. Your Honour, may I just show you a photograph that shows such a stall since we are talking about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We are going to come to that. I'm going to show it. Well, actually I am giving up on this particular matter. The next day, when you came, did you notice a stall whose surface, the top surface, was damaged as if something had exploded there? Did you notice that when you came the following day?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, when something explodes on a wooden surface, when 2.3 kilograms of TNT blows up on a wooden surface, there would be nothing left of that surface. This is my experience, experience on the basis of my practice and of the colleagues from the VTI who worked with me on these experiments and the testing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at 1D3296, 1D3296, please. First question,

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is any of these stalls turned on its roof?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you. Can you point out which one you're thinking of?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you don't see it, all right. Never mind. Can you see that this man is pointing to the wooden board and there is a defective part on it?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you tell me which part you're pointing to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's marked C2, the board is marked as C2.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On C2, I don't see any defects.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where this red bag is standing, that's where it is.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not seeing it. What is a defect in your eyes? You're not being precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at D1? Are there any defects there? I mean, you know what a defect is, that a part of the board would be missing.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. A small part on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And here on C2, where you see some sort of red bag there, do you see a part of the board missing there?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't make any kind of conclusion because, first of all, I don't know what that stall originally looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about this stall? Do you know that there are two double lines on the roof so this stall is turned over and it's burned? There are burn marks on it. And a part of the panel is missing. This is the one that's marked D1.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, the effect of burning on the wood? What does that mean to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, can you look at the bottom where it says, D1, or O1, at the bottom where we have two parallel pipes? Is that the roof construction of the stall?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, I couldn't say. I cannot conclude that on the basis of this. You cannot make me make a conclusion on the basis of something that I'm not seeing very well. What is the point of this whole story?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the base of the roof broader than the bottom of the board -- of the stall?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm going to show you some stalls as well. Here they are. These are the stalls from Markale that I photographed. Here they are. If we want to discuss that particular matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I'm asking you to look at this particular stall. This was published in the special review of Sandzak, and an eyewitness there is pointing out certain objects. I assert that this particular stall, with two parallel pipes at the bottom, I'm saying that that is the roof and that the bottom is facing up. It's turned upside down. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you're asking me -- well, first of all, I would like to know who is it from Sandzak that photographed this? I can show you what I saw and photographed and I can discuss the photographs that I looked at. I can proffer that photograph and we can discuss that hypothesis of yours that the projectile hit the wood panel of the stall at a height of 90 degrees -- 90 -- 0.90 metres from the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 1D3297? This is the section of the footage marked V 000350-1-A, and the photograph is 1D3297. Thank you. Can you see this stall construction and can you see the results of the damage caused by the explosion? On the actual wooden panel, below this letter A, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the effects of fragmentation. Do you know what happens when a fragment of five grams hits a surface at 1200 metres per second? So 100 metres velocity. Newton metres velocity is sometimes taken into account for artillery that is supposed to incapacitate a horse that is dragging artillery. That is one value. But here, the value of the metre-Newtons is much, much higher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm only amazed by the ability of our interpreters, if you could slow down, doctor, when you are speaking some technical issues. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue. Okay. It's time to take another five-minute break. Five minutes. --- Break taken at 3.56 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, let's finish this issue about the stalls. If an explosive device would explode or, rather, in order to have the stall turned upside down on the spot, does that mean that the explosion had to happen underneath? If it happened next to it, it would eject it to the side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, whether something is going to turn upside down or not depends on the pressure and the surface to which -- that is exposed to this pressure. Therefore, I cannot give you an answer unless you give me a precise definition and tell me where the explosive device was, what was the volume of the explosive, what was below the explosive device, what kind of material, et cetera, because, Mr. Karadzic, after an explosion occurred, a rescue operation was mounted to save the wounded and to take away the dead and during that operation the stalls could have been turned upside down. So there is a human factor involved there, not only explosion. So you're asking me to comment something, these people are just standing there and looking at something and I don't know what had happened before that, therefore I don't think it's technically appropriate for me to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go back to what you were doing. You decided on the angle of impact by the stabiliser, is that a modified method and what is the degree of its accuracy?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, since World War II --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please don't give us a lecture. My question was not properly recorded. You determined the descent angle of the shell; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I determined that angle in a very simple fashion. I put the support of the stabiliser inside the hole that was caused by the penetration of the stabiliser through the ground, I put the military quadrant and I determined that the angle was 60 degrees, and I allowed for a margin of error of plus/minus 5 degrees. So that's a standard method that is applied. If you claim that I made a mistake, the error could have been only expressed in minutes, that's why I allowed for this margin of error of plus/minus 5 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Has this method been verified and does it have a reputation of being accurate? Is it recognised?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a method to be recognised --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this particular one. Don't give us lecture. I'm asking you: Is this a standard and verified and recognised method and is it accurate?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it was not normal practice to kill people at marketplace. I haven't finished, Mr. Karadzic, please. I have never interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to give you an answer, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's hear the answer out. Dr. Zecevic, could you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Give me more time, Excellency, and then I will be prepared to listen to him. Give me 25 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Once asked, he should answer your question. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This was not a standard method. It became a standard after the capture of Baghdad by the USA, and one can deem this method to be already adopted in assessing the operations carried out by terrorists in urban zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the source of the verification of this method from an expert and scientific point of view?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I can give you that, and I can show you in what way according to the US regulations, and based on the canal created by the projectile fuse at the time of explosion, a direction can be established. However, there is no need to determine the descent angle of the stabiliser for a very simple reason. In military methodology, we can determine where artillery fire is coming from, and in this particular instance, it was completely irrelevant for the army to determine the location of the origin of fire. So what we have here is military forensic methodology and it's going to be introduced and applied in the cases when we want to investigate whether civilian targets were targeted intentionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that it is said in the manuals that the stabiliser serves only to identify the projectile that came in and exploded?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said just now that the stabiliser serves for determining the direction from which a shell comes, but not the -- it is used for the descent angle, because that's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not what I said, or maybe I got confused. I can repeat what I really think. I need the permission by the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means, yes. Proceed, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The direction of the projectile, from which it came, after the explosion takes place is determined based on the effects of the fragments on the ground, and based on the canal made by the fuse which is in the top section of the projectile and which is embedded into the ground at the point of impact. This is what is said in military manuals. In this particular case, it was extremely important for us to determine at which angle the projectile fell, and for that purpose, I put the support of the stabiliser that it made and by using a military instrument to determine the angle at which it fell. So this is nothing technically complicated or unrealistic. However, the very presence of the stabiliser in the ground, and the -- its angle can clearly indicate the zones from which the projectile was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read you your previous answer. It starts from line 8 on page 44 and then line 11: [In English] "However, there is no need to determine the descent angle of the stabiliser for a very simple reason: In military methodology, we can determine where artillery fire is coming from and in this particular -- it was completely irrelevant for the army to determine the location of the original fire." [Interpretation] That was your answer. Now I'm asking you. You got engaged in determining the angle in order to determine that it had come from the Serb-held territory rather than from the Muslim-held territory.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, may I answer this question in the manner I think would be appropriate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't do that in order to rule out a position that was in the BH Army-controlled territory. Now, with full responsibility, I can tell you that because I put this in my report, an order was issued for me to be assassinated in 1994, and the person who was to kill me is known. His name is known. Because I specified that there was a location in the BH Army-controlled territory as a possible origin of fire. So my life was at stake in Sarajevo all the time. I could have been killed. Now, after this kind of discussions and conversations and certain propaganda programmes broadcast by VRS, I'm not sure whether I would again be the target of assassination when I go back to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did this threat lead you to deal with distances of 3 or 4.000 metres and that on the basis of the angle that you determined, you concluded that it had come from the Serbian side? And can you tell us who is it that is threatening you?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm not afraid to put in writing what I wanted to put in writing, and that's what I did. Everything that I wrote in my report is identical to what experts of the Military Technical Institute in 2003 did. They only said in their analysis that the ground on Markale was made of concrete in order to demonstrate that the descent angle was not within the realistic sphere.
